title: Majority: win or draw, then which pawn
outcomes: Decides whether a pawn majority wins or only draws before choosing a move
Chooses the first pawn move and checks it against the Black king's position
Recognises a wing where equal pawn numbers give no majority

steps.text: *Pawn majorities: the candidate and the kings* showed that the candidate usually leads. Now decide before you move: **win or draw?** Count the majority, then find the enemy king. If it stands in front of your pawns, the natural push can draw. Then pick the first move and *check it*.

steps.caption: White to move: three pawns against two on the kingside. The Black king stands in front of them.

line.say: f3 keeps the win, though it is neither the candidate nor the middle pawn. h4 or h3 only draw; g4 loses.

claims.statement: White has three pawns on the kingside.
Black has two pawns on the kingside.
After h4 the result for White is only a draw.
After h3 the result for White is only a draw.

steps.text: **Conditions.** A majority wins when it can make a passed pawn that the enemy king cannot stop in time. That depends on the kings, not only on the count. **Rule of thumb:** the candidate leads, the middle pawn waits, *unless* the enemy king stands in front: then calculate. With equal pawns on the wing there is no majority to convert.

steps.title: Same first move, three positions
steps.prompt: White plays a4 (the candidate) in each position. Predict the result with best play, then check.

Rate how sure you were (low / medium / high) that your majority would win. Then name the square where the enemy king stood in the position you found hardest, and say whether you looked at it before choosing the candidate.
